newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Rebels starts freeing hostages in Tajikistan - Tass.
newsitem.headline: Rebels starts freeing hostages in Tajikistan - Tass.

text.p: The leader of a rebel Islamic group holding 14 hostages in Tajikistan said on Friday he had begun to release the captives in exchange for other rebels, Russia's Itar-Tass news agency reported.

The agency said rebel leader Bakhram Sadirov had told Russian Deputy Prime Minister Vitaly Ignatenko by telephone at 1430 GMT that the hostage-for-rebel swap had started. The report could not immediately be confirmed independently.
Tass said two women hostages -- reporters from Tass and Interfax news agency -- were already heading out of the rebel camp with a driver for Russia's NTV television network.
Other hostages would be released after the Tajik government handed over a group of rebels in exchange, the report said.

The rebels' main condition for releasing the hostages, seized more than a week ago, has been for Tajik authorities to fly in rebel comrades from neighbouring Afghanistan and allow the two groups to meet up.
The hostages include three U.N. observers -- two from Switzerland and one from Ukraine -- four Russian journalists and four workers with the U.N. refugee agency.
